content.title: About
content.content: Apple cobbler is a classic American dessert made of baked apples topped with a biscuit‑like dough that forms a golden, crumbly crust. The apples become soft and fragrant, while the topping turns crisp and buttery.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cobbler originated in the 19th‑century United States, inspired by British pies.
Tart apple varieties such as Granny Smith are traditionally used to keep a slight acidity.
The topping is usually leavened with baking powder or simply relies on the lightness of flour and butter, not yeast.
Variations include adding berries (blueberries, raspberries) or dried fruits.
Cobbler is often served warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Apples provide both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Apples supply vitamin C, which aids the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The cobbler topping is typically made with a modest amount of butter, keeping the dessert relatively low‑fat.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Apple skins contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index
items.content: Baked apples have a lower glycemic impact than many other sweet desserts.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Cobbler is often sweetened, so people monitoring blood sugar should watch portion size.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: The topping contains wheat flour, which can be problematic for those with celiac disease or gluten intolerance.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While not overly fatty, a serving can be calorie‑dense due to sugar and butter.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cobbler warm, typically with a scoop of vanilla ice cream, whipped cream, or yogurt. It can be eaten straight from the baking dish or plated individually.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in the microwave or oven before serving to restore the crisp topping.
